An outdoor world at street level in a real place: 9 Ainslie Pl, Edinburgh EH3 6AT, UK. Open sky overhead. This is a continuous exterior environment that continues in every direction, not an enclosed courtyard and not a picture.

The viewpoint is about 4 metres up, at upper-storey height.

THE PLACE
architectural documentary survey of the Regency classical crescent facade at Ainslie Place, Edinburgh, designed by James Gillespie Graham. Concave curved sweep of 3-storey and basement terraced townhouses constructed from pale buff-grey Craigleith sandstone.

STRUCTURE AND MASSING
Category A listed Regency neoclassical concave circus terrace designed by James Gillespie Graham (1822) forming the Moray Estate crescent. Massing follows a 3-storey plus attic and submerged basement configuration, flanked by advanced 4-storey terminal pavilions.

SURFACES AND MATERIALS
Primary facade: Craigleith quartzitic sandstone ashlar, displaying authentic urban sulfur-dioxide gypsum crusts in sheltered cornices and light surface micro-abrasions from North Sea maritime exposure. Area railings and ironwork: Wrought and cast iron spearhead balustrades, urn finials, and integral overthrow lantern brackets finished in semi-gloss black enamel.

VEGETATION
Ainslie Place central pleasure gardens feature mature deciduous urban parkland canopy anchored by *Acer pseudoplatanus*

ILLUMINATION
Direct sunlight from a true compass bearing of 251 degrees at 21.4 degrees elevation above the horizon, casting hard shadows away from that bearing at a length consistent with that sun elevation. Light colour temperature approximately 4500K. Clear sky.

OCCUPANCY
No people and no vehicles anywhere. Retain permanent civil fabric: kerbs, railings, street lamps, steps, gates, and mature trees.
